endpoints.description: Health check - confirms the API is reachable.
Log in with username/password and obtain a JWT Bearer token, valid for 15 minutes.

Returns the username embedded in the caller's JWT access token. Reads the identity directly from the token claims rather than the database, so it still answers even if the user row backing the token has since been deleted.

Lists user accounts. The underlying listing query depends on a page-scoped 'current user' concept that a bearer-token request never populates, so this always returns an empty users array regardless of caller role.

Creates a new user account by invoking 'opencli user-add' with the given username, password, email and plan. Rejects usernames listed in the forbidden-usernames file (case-insensitive) and requires email, username, password and plan_name.
Returns detailed account information for a single user: profile fields, plan limits, owned domains, sites, and current disk/inode usage (read from the quota report, matched by exact username).
Creates a new user account. Behaves identically to POST /api/users -- the {username} path segment is ignored, only the JSON body's own 'username' field is used.
Changes a user's plan by invoking 'opencli user-change_plan' with the new plan name.

response.message: Plan for user bob changed to pro.

endpoints.description: Updates a user's password (via 'opencli user-password') or suspends/unsuspends the account (via 'opencli user-suspend'/'user-unsuspend'), depending on which of 'password' or 'action' is present in the body.
Deletes a user account by invoking 'opencli user-delete <username> -y'. Requires a JSON Content-Type even though no body fields are read.

Generates a one-time admin_token file and returns a signed autologin link that the user-panel's /login_autologin route uses to sign the caller in as this user. Exists as a dedicated route rather than an HTTP-method dispatch on /api/users/{username} because CONNECT-style addressing doesn't fit an ordinary path-based resource.
Lists all domains registered on the server.

Adds a new domain for a user by invoking 'opencli domains-add <domain> <username> --docroot <docroot>'. docroot defaults to /var/www/html/<domain> if omitted, and must always fall under /var/www/html/.

response.stdout: Domain example.com added successfully for user bob.

endpoints.description: Manual dispatcher for two-segment /api/domains/* routes that would otherwise overlap in Go's ServeMux. Based on the seg2/seg3 values it delegates to: GET docroot for a domain (seg2='docroot'), the DNS zone file (seg3='dns'), the Caddy config snippet (seg3='caddy'), SSL status/info (seg3='ssl'), or the JSON access log (seg3='log'); any other combination returns 404. Each sub-route has its own response shape -- see the docroot example below for the 'docroot' case.

Manual dispatcher for two-segment /api/domains/* POST routes. Based on the seg2/seg3 values it delegates to: setting a domain's docroot (seg2='docroot'), saving the DNS zone file (seg3='dns'), saving the Caddy config (seg3='caddy'), managing SSL (seg3='ssl'), or -- as the default/fallback case -- a domain lifecycle action (suspend/unsuspend/delete) where seg2 is the action and seg3 is the domain, invoking 'opencli domains-<action> <domain>'.
Returns the raw webserver vhost config file content for a domain, read from the user's docker-data webserver volume (404 if the user has no resolvable context or the file doesn't exist).
Replaces the raw webserver vhost config file for a domain and restarts the user's webserver container to apply it (a failed restart still counts as a successful save).

response.message: VirtualHosts file for example.com saved successfully and nginx restarted.

endpoints.description: Returns the current contents of the default nginx/openresty/apache/varnish/caddy domain config templates and the default/suspended-user/suspended-website landing pages used for new domains.
Updates one or more of the domain config templates. Each present, non-null key must be a string; any subset of the known template keys may be supplied and only those are written to disk.
Returns the pre-generated GoAccess HTML stats report for a domain, read from the user's stats directory. Data is regenerated every 24 hours; a 404 is returned if no report has been generated yet.

Lists all hosting plans. Unlike the HTML admin pages, this carries no role gate beyond a valid token -- reseller-scoping of the plan list depends on a page-scoped 'current user' concept a bearer token never populates, so every authenticated caller (admin, user, or reseller) sees every plan.

Creates a new hosting plan by invoking 'opencli plan-create' with the given fields (all default to 0/'1'/'default' when omitted). If the acting token belongs to a reseller, the plan is created scoped to that reseller.
Returns a single plan's details by numeric ID. Routes with a non-numeric plan_id never reach this handler and are reported as a plain 404.

Edits an existing plan by invoking 'opencli plan-edit' with the given fields. name/description fall back to the literal string 'None' when omitted (mirroring the CLI's own convention); other numeric fields default to '0'/'1'/'100'/'default'.
Same handler as PUT /api/plans/{plan_id} -- partially or fully edits an existing plan via 'opencli plan-edit'.
Deletes a plan by numeric ID via 'opencli plan-delete <id> --json'.

Returns the user's rendered podman-compose configuration (the raw 'podman-compose ... config' output, passed through as-is), or -- when a non-empty ?stats= query value is given -- a live 'podman stats' snapshot of all the user's containers instead. On lookup/config failure this still returns 200 with an {"error":...} body rather than a JSON error status, mirroring the underlying CLI helper.

Manages a single container. action must be one of start, stop, restart, cpu, ram, or pids. start/stop toggle the container (start optionally accepts 'pull' to re-pull the image first); restart restarts it; cpu/ram/pids set the corresponding resource limit from the JSON or form field 'value'.

Returns the current DNS cluster configuration: the allow-transfer and also-notify IP lists parsed from the BIND config, whether clustering is enabled, and the raw config file content. If the config can't be read, still returns 200 with an {"error":...} body.

Manages the DNS cluster based on the 'action' field: 'enable'/'disable' toggle clustering, 'create' adds a slave IP (validated as a reachable IPv4 address via rndc, then triggers an async zone sync to it), and 'delete' removes a slave IP from the config. Restarts the DNS service after enable/disable/create/delete.

response.message: IP 192.0.2.12 added to DNS cluster successfully.

endpoints.description: Checks reachability/status of a DNS cluster slave node: first tries 'rndc status' against it, then falls back to running 'uname -a' over SSH if rndc doesn't respond with a recognizable status.
Returns the default IPv4 and IPv6 BIND zone file templates used for new domains.
Updates the default IPv4 and/or IPv6 zone file templates. Either or both of zone_template_ipv4/zone_template_ipv6 may be supplied; only the supplied ones are written to disk.

Returns the mail server's overall status: webmail status/domain, mailserver container status, total email account count, the parsed mailserver.env configuration, and the current email storage location.

Updates one recognized mail server setting per call: storage_type/email_storage_location, webmail_domain, webmail_software, or one or more ENABLE_* checkbox flags (e.g. ENABLE_CLAMAV, ENABLE_FAIL2BAN, ENABLE_POP3). Toggling a checkbox flag restarts the mailserver in the background.

response.message: Configuration updated! Fail2Ban and ClamAV require Mailserver to be recreated. Make sure to stop&start the service.

endpoints.description: Lists all mailserver email accounts with their quotas; returns an empty list with a non-running status if the mailserver container isn't up.
Performs one account-management action, selected by the 'action' field: 'password' (change password), 'quota-set', 'quota-del', or 'restrict' (add/remove a send or receive restriction).
Deletes one or more email accounts given in the 'emails' array.
Returns the current Postfix mail queue contents along with the mailserver's running status.
Retries or deletes queued mail. 'action' is 'retry' or 'delete'; 'scope' is 'all' or 'selected' (with 'queue_ids' listing specific queue IDs when scope is 'selected').

Returns configured postfwd rate-limit rules and known usernames, plus the raw postfwd config content. If a '?hits=<domain>' query parameter is given instead, returns the recent rate-limit hit log lines for that domain.

response.raw_content: id=limit_acme_acme_com ; sender=~.+@acme.com ; protocol_state==RCPT ; rate=30/3600 ; action=550 Rate limit exceeded

endpoints.description: Manages postfwd rate-limit rules: either writes raw postfwd config directly via 'raw_content', or performs an 'action' of update-domain, reset-domain, reset-user, reset-all, delete-domain, delete-user, or delete-all.
Returns the current HTTP Basic Auth protection settings configured for OpenAdmin itself.
Updates HTTP Basic Auth settings for OpenAdmin (enabled flag, username, password); any provided fields are written to config and OpenAdmin is flagged for restart.

response.message: Basic_auth settings for OpenAdmin edited successfully.

endpoints.description: Returns whether the blacklisted-useragents feature is enabled and the current blacklist file contents.
Updates the blacklisted user-agents list and/or the enabled flag; flags OpenPanel for restart if anything changed.
Disables OpenAdmin entirely (runs 'opencli admin off' in the background), after which OpenAdmin must be managed via terminal.

response.message: OpenAdmin is now disabled and all further actions need to be performed via terminal.

endpoints.description: Reports whether the ConfigServer Firewall (csf) command is available on the host.
Passes an arbitrary set of key=value parameters through to csf.pl (written to a temp file and executed) and returns its raw output; mirrors the CSF admin iframe's query-string plumbing.

response.output: ConfigServer Firewall: IP added to allow list

endpoints.description: Returns whether CorazaWAF is enabled and a summary count of total/active/inactive WAF rule sets.
Enables or disables CorazaWAF, given status 'yes' or 'no'; then returns the same status/rule-set summary as the GET.
Lists every WAF rule set file with its name, path, non-empty line count, and on/off status.
Enables or disables a single WAF rule set by name, renaming its .conf/.conf.disabled file accordingly. Caddy must be restarted afterward to apply changes.

response.message: Rules set enabled. Restart Caddy to apply changes.

endpoints.description: Returns the caller's own TOTP 2FA status. If 2FA is already enabled, returns only that flag; if not, mints and returns a brand-new TOTP secret and QR code data URI for enrollment on every call (stateless, no session caching).
Enables TOTP 2FA for the caller's own account after validating the submitted code against the given secret.
Disables TOTP 2FA for the caller's own account after verifying the account password.

Lists the caller's own registered passkeys (id, optional name, created_at), newest first. Registering a new passkey isn't supported over this JSON API since it requires a browser/authenticator round trip.
Renames one of the caller's own passkeys, identified by id (must belong to the caller).
Deletes one of the caller's own passkeys, identified by id (must belong to the caller).
Returns the raw parsed contents of the monitored-services config file (services.json) verbatim, whatever shape it happens to be.
Overwrites the monitored-services config file wholesale with the JSON request body (pretty-printed before writing).

Returns every monitored service flagged on_dashboard, each as its full config entry plus a live 'status' field ('Active', 'Inactive', or 'Error: ...' if the underlying check failed). Docker-type services are checked via a single 'podman ps' call; others via systemctl is-active.

Starts, stops, or restarts one monitored service by name (action is one of start/restart/stop). Docker-backed services (e.g. caddy, openpanel, mailserver) are managed via podman-compose up/down; all others via the generic 'service <name> <action>' command. Only services flagged on_dashboard in services.json may be targeted.
Returns the raw JSON output of 'podman info --format json', passed through unmodified.
Returns every account's dedicated IP address, keyed by username, read from each account's own ip.json file (accounts with no such file are omitted).
Returns a snapshot of host system information: hostname, OS, kernel version, CPU model, uptime (seconds), running process count, OpenPanel version, and available package updates count.
Returns per-core CPU usage percentages from a 1-second blocking sample, keyed by core name.
Returns current RAM usage: raw byte figures (total/available/used/percent) plus a human-readable version of the same figures.
Returns disk usage for every mounted filesystem (excluding pseudo-filesystems, /snap, and podman storage), each with device, mountpoint, fstype, and total/used/free bytes plus used percent.
Returns per-user disk and inode quota usage, keyed by username, read from the quota report file (generated on demand via 'opencli user-quota' if missing). Bandwidth fields are always hardcoded to 0.
Returns all notification log lines, newest first, with blank lines skipped; creates an empty log file if none exists yet.

Marks one notification as read, identified by its 1-indexed line_number counted from the newest (bottom-of-file) entry; if a 'command=mark_all_as_read' query param or JSON body field is given instead, marks every notification as read.
Deletes one notification, identified by its 1-indexed line_number counted from the newest entry; if a 'command=delete_all' query param or JSON body field is given instead, deletes every notification.
Lists every parsed line of the managed crontab (line number, schedule, command, and logging flag); returns null if the crontab file is missing.
Rewrites the schedule and logging flag of one or more existing crontab lines, identified by line number, reusing the same cron-line rewriting logic as the HTML /server/crons page.
Returns the current sshd service status, the raw sshd_config contents, the list of authorized_keys entries, and the parsed basic settings (port, password/pubkey auth, permit root login).

response.config:
Port 22
PasswordAuthentication yes
PubkeyAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin yes

endpoints.description: Performs exactly one SSH-management action per request, chosen by priority order from the body: control the sshd service (action), overwrite the raw sshd_config (config), add an authorized key (new_key), remove an authorized key (key_to_remove), or update basic settings (port/password_auth/pubkey_auth/permit_root_login). Unlike the HTML form equivalent, only the first matching field is acted on and the response names exactly which operation ran.
Returns the raw contents of sshd_config as a single string.

response.config:
Port 22
PasswordAuthentication yes
PubkeyAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin yes

endpoints.description: Overwrites sshd_config with the supplied raw text and restarts the SSH service to apply it.

body.config:
Port 22
PasswordAuthentication yes
PubkeyAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin yes

response.message: SSH configuration updated and service restarted.

endpoints.description: Returns the server's currently configured timezone (read via `timedatectl`, falling back to /etc/localtime) plus the full list of available IANA timezone names.
Changes the server's system timezone via `timedatectl set-timezone`, after validating the requested value is a known timezone name.
Drops the Linux page/dentry/inode caches by running `sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches`, freeing cached (but reclaimable) RAM.
Clears swap by running `swapoff -a && swapon -a` in the background (fire-and-forget); the response is returned immediately with HTTP 202 before the cycle necessarily completes.
Returns the clustering default-node configuration (default_node host and default_ssh_key_path) along with whether an SSH connection to that node currently validates successfully.
Updates the clustering default_node and/or default_ssh_key_path config values; if both are supplied together, validates the SSH connection to the node before saving.
Lists all running system processes parsed from /proc (PID, name, CPU%, memory%, priority, owner, command), sorted by the given criterion (default: CPU descending).
Performs an action on a specific process by PID. Only the 'kill' action is permitted via this API route (no strace/streaming support here, unlike the HTML process manager page).

DANGEROUS: changes the server's root Linux user password (via `passwd root`) and verifies the change took effect. Restricted to the super-admin role since it grants full root shell/SSH access to whoever knows the new password.

DANGEROUS: reboots or hard-crashes the physical/virtual server. 'graceful' schedules a normal `reboot` after a 15s delay; 'hard' schedules writing to /proc/sysrq-trigger after a 10s delay, forcibly resetting the machine without a clean shutdown. This call blocks until the delay elapses and the command runs, and can be disabled entirely via a flag file (/root/disable_openadmin_reboot_ui), in which case it returns 403.
Lightweight liveness probe used to detect when the server has come back up after a reboot; simply confirms the OpenAdmin API is reachable and responding.

Polls the status of a background `opencli server-migrate` run: 'running' while the recorded PID is still alive, 'finished' once it has exited, or 'unknown' if no migration has been started (no pid file). Also returns the accumulated log output.

Starts a background server-to-server migration (`opencli server-migrate`) that copies data from a remote source server to this one, given the remote host, its root user, and its password. All three fields are required.
Lists all administrator accounts (users with a non-reseller role), including last login IP/time, 2FA status, and whether passkeys are registered.

Runs one administrator-account action (create/reset_password/rename_user/suspend/unsuspend/delete/disable_2fa/disable_passkeys) selected by the 'action' field, reusing the same opencli/admindb plumbing as the HTML administrators page.

response.message: Successfully created a new admin user: newadmin

endpoints.description: Lists all reseller accounts with account/disk quota usage and allowed plans; a reseller caller is rejected with 403 (only admins may list other resellers).

Runs one reseller-account action (create/reset_password/rename_user/update/suspend/unsuspend/delete/disable_2fa/disable_passkeys); a caller with the reseller role can only ever reset their own password through this endpoint regardless of the submitted action/username.
Returns the current general server settings: the user-panel and admin-panel ports, the reverse-proxy backend, the forced admin domain, and whether dev mode is on.

Updates general server settings (domain, ports, proxy backend, dev mode); applies only the values that changed, writes OpenPanel/OpenAdmin restart-needed flag files as appropriate, and reports which settings were changed.
Returns the grouped default .env values for new accounts, the available PHP versions data, and the list of available vs. currently active autostart services.

Updates key/value entries in the default .env file (rewriting matching keys in place, uncommenting/commenting PROXY_HTTP_PORT based on VARNISH) and, if 'services' is provided, replaces the autostart-services file with the valid subset of the submitted list.
Returns the raw contents of the default account-template .env and docker-compose.yml files.
Overwrites the default .env and/or docker-compose.yml template files with the submitted raw content (each field applied only when present and non-null).
Resets the default .env and docker-compose.yml template files by re-fetching both from their canonical GitHub source; reports per-file errors instead of failing outright if only one fetch fails.

response.message: Defaults reset successfully from remote source!

endpoints.description: Returns the raw .env and docker-compose.yml contents from a specific user's home directory (resolved from {username} via their docker context).
Overwrites the .env and/or docker-compose.yml files in a specific user's home directory with the submitted content, then returns the resulting file contents.
Lists the names of all feature sets visible to the acting user: global feature sets plus the acting reseller's own (a reseller only sees their own sets).
Creates a new, empty feature set file named by 'feature_name' (in the global directory for admins, or the acting reseller's own directory for resellers); fails if a set with that name already exists.
Returns the enabled modules for the given feature set plus the full feature/plugin catalog, each entry annotated with its enabled ('status') and module-availability ('module_enabled') state.

Applies an action to a feature set: 'update' replaces its enabled feature list, 'enable_all'/'disable_all' toggle every known feature, or 'delete' removes the set (rejected for the 'default' set or a set still in use by a hosting package).
Lists translation locales available on GitHub, marking which are installed locally and which one is the current default.
Either installs a new locale ('locale' field) by downloading its translation files, or sets the panel's default locale ('default' field); exactly one of the two fields is expected per call.
Returns the full module/feature catalog (each entry annotated with its enabled status) and the list of installed plugins.

Replaces the enabled_modules list in the modules config file, toggles the phpmyadmin/clamav docker-compose services to match, generates the DNS rndc key if a DNS module was newly enabled, and flags OpenPanel for restart.

Returns the raw contents of every custom-code file (custom CSS/JS, header/footer snippets, startup/post-update scripts, forbidden usernames, restricted domains, how-to guides, WordPress theme/plugin sets, PageSpeed API key), keyed by field name.

Writes any of the custom-code fields present as string values in the body to their corresponding files and flags OpenPanel for restart. Unlike the HTML page, this API endpoint applies no Enterprise-license/reseller-role gating on the Enterprise-only fields (custom_css, custom_js, in_header, in_footer, custom_section, howto_guides).
Returns the raw contents of the global PHP options.txt file plus each PHP version's php.ini file, keyed by 'options' and version keys like 'php81'.
Overwrites the global PHP options.txt and/or one or more per-version php.ini files with the submitted string content; reports which keys were actually updated.
Proxies Caddy's local admin API /metrics endpoint verbatim as a text/plain Prometheus-format body; a fetch failure or non-2xx upstream status is reported as a 500 plaintext error message instead.
endpoints.response:
# HELP caddy_admin_http_requests_total Counter of requests made to the Admin API's HTTP endpoints.
caddy_admin_http_requests_total{...} 42

endpoints.description: Returns the current update config (autoupdate/autopatch settings), the latest available panel version, and the recent update log entries.
Sets the auto-update preference (one of minor_and_major, minor_only, major_only, none), rewriting the corresponding autoupdate/autopatch on/off flags in the update config file.
Kicks off an immediate panel update in the background (no request body); returns immediately once the update process has been started, not once it has finished.
Lists available OpenPanel docker image tags/versions fetched from Docker Hub.
Pins the panel to a specific version: writes the version into the compose .env file, pulls that image tag, and runs docker-compose up to switch to it (used for downgrades as well as pinned upgrades).
Returns the notification email/SMTP settings, the SSH allowlist, and the full notifications config (thresholds, HTTP limits, per-action toggles).

Updates notification thresholds, HTTP connection limits, webhook URL, notification email, SMTP settings, per-action/default toggles, and the SSH allowlist -- each field is applied only when present (and changed) in the JSON body, and a malformed SSH allowlist entry (invalid IP/CIDR) fails the whole request with a 400.
Reads the currently configured license key by running `opencli license key --json` and returns it verbatim (trimmed).
Sets/activates a new license key by running `opencli license <key> --json --no-restart`, which validates the key against the licensing server before applying it.
Removes the currently configured license key by running `opencli license delete --json`.
Returns details about the currently active license by running `opencli license info --json`. Wired directly to LicensePage.ServeLicenseInfo, whose JSON shape is identical to this API route.

Re-verifies the current license against the licensing server by running `opencli license verify --json`. Wired directly to LicensePage.ServeLicenseVerify, whose JSON shape is identical to this API route.

Generates a public, non-interactive diagnostics report by running `opencli report --public --non-interactive` and returns its output as JSON text (not a downloadable file -- writeJSON sets Content-Type: application/json and the report text is embedded in the "message" field).

Lists import log files (with derived status) for a given backup panel type. `panel_type` must be one of "cpanel" or "cyberpanel" (unlike the HTML /import/{panel_type} route, "openpanel" restores are not exposed here -- see /user/import instead); any other value returns 400.
Starts an import of a cPanel or CyberPanel backup into a new OpenPanel account, cloning/running the import script for the given backup path and target hosting plan in the background.

response.message: Import process from /root/backup-user.tar.gz (CyberPanel backup) has started.

endpoints.description: Returns the raw contents of a single account-import log file as JSON. `{log_filename...}` is a Go 1.22+ wildcard path segment and may contain slashes (a nested relative path under the import log directory); a path that resolves outside that directory, or a missing/non-file target, returns 404.

Performs a shallow (non-recursive) scan of /, /home, and /root for cPanel/CyberPanel (backup-*.tar.gz) or OpenPanel (<user>_<date>_<time>.tar.gz) style backup archives and returns the matched absolute paths as a flat array. Delegates to the same logic as the HTML admin /json/backup-files route.

Lists every OpenPanel-to-OpenPanel transfer log file (*.log) directly under the transfer log directory, as a flat array of file paths. Delegates to the same logic as the HTML admin /json/transfers route.

Starts a live OpenPanel-to-OpenPanel account transfer in the background by running `opencli user-transfer` with the given target account, host, and SSH credentials. If the target server is an IP (not a domain), it also configures iptables for the transfer.

response.message: Transfer process for account newuser started in the background.

endpoints.description: Scans the transfer log directory for logs belonging to a given OpenPanel username and reports each transfer's current status (derived from the log's PID/SUCCESS markers and whether that PID is still alive). A "SUSPENDED_" prefix on the username is stripped before scanning, mirroring the suspended-account naming convention used elsewhere.

Returns the raw contents of a single transfer log file as JSON. `{log_filename...}` is a Go 1.22+ wildcard path segment and may contain slashes (a nested relative path under the transfer log directory); a path that resolves outside that directory, or a missing/non-file target, returns 404.
